parsed.why: No criminalisation, functioning rule of law, Pride and gay venues; but no gender-identity service protection, media hostility, toilet backlash, unregistration of LGBT groups, and border treatment undocumented.

Anti-discrimination law expressly covering gender identity in public establishments, self-ID recognition, marriage equality, bias penalties and an openly gay head of government; enforcement machinery and hate-crime classification remain incomplete.

Strong paper protections — constitutional and criminal anti-discrimination on gender identity — undercut by documented non-investigation of LGBT murders, a 2024 survey recording widespread exclusion, and only minority support for trans rights.

Hate speech and discrimination laws cover gender identity, self-ID recognition, exemplary prosecution of a Pride mass shooting and supportive government; offset by rising reports, 8% reporting rate, falling clearance and concentrated extremist hostility.

Decriminalised, Gender Equality Act 2019 covering gender identity across all spheres plus official sensitisation, judicial conduct code, no recorded LGBT abuses; thin visitor-facing data and no documented acceptance or enforcement record.
